subject: Request for SLA reconciliation: degraded API reachability during CDN control-plane upgrade
messages:
From: Matthew Park <matthew.park@calypsohealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgePartners Support <ops@edgepartners.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Degraded reachability during EdgePartners control-plane upgrade — request for SLA reconciliation

Hi Vanessa,

We saw elevated 5xx rates and timeouts for the Redwood API between 2027-06-10T02:10:00Z and 2027-06-10T02:43:00Z (UTC). Our paging showed partial failures for a subset of backend requests that route through EdgePartners POPs in us-west and us-central. The issues coincided with a control-plane upgrade notice from EdgePartners (they posted a short announcement at 02:05Z).

This resulted in degraded response rates for our patient-matching endpoint (90th p50 latency spiked from 85ms to 610ms, and success rate dropped from 99.95% to ~96.2% for that 33-minute window). Our contract references availability measured at the API endpoint and excludes scheduled maintenance only when Redwood initiates it or notifies us 72 hours in advance. We did not receive a direct maintenance notice from Redwood.

We attached a condensed packet of our traces and synthetic probe logs (calypso_evidence_snapshot.zip) and a short CSV with aggregated error rates. Calypso is requesting a formal reconciliation of the uptime window, the method used to apportion credits in partial degradations, and whether this event is excluded as a third-party maintenance event.

Please escalate if needed — this is impacting an upcoming go-live. Looking for a timeline for investigation and an estimate of any credits that will be provided.

Thanks,
Matthew Park
Director, Platform Reliability
Calypso Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Degraded reachability during EdgePartners control-plane upgrade — request for SLA reconciliation

Vanessa / Karthik — I pulled request traces, router decision logs, and a sample of the KV cache eviction trace for the 02:00–03:00Z horizon. Quick summary:

- Redwood received a burst of 502/504s and elevated tail latency from ~02:09:40Z; request routing traces show a concentrated error rate from POPs that peer via EdgePartners in us-west-2 and us-central-1.
- For roughly 18 of the 33 minutes, our runtime performed dynamic path-fallbacks (shifted traffic to secondary egress) which reduced error rate but increased tail latency due to cold-KV penalties on some model routes.
- EdgePartners’ public bulletin indicates a control-plane upgrade starting 02:05Z; their maintenance notes imply transient reconfiguration of BGP sessions leading to packet reordering on a subset of lanes.

Interpretation: this is a blended incident — a third-party control-plane upgrade created noisy conditions; Redwood’s smart routing partially mitigated availability loss but inadvertently exposed Calypso to latency spikes because of cache misses and longer egress paths. Contractually, our SLA language excludes third-party maintenance when we can attribute outage to the third party and the customer received either (a) notification from the third party or (b) Redwood provided reasonable notice. We do not have a record that Redwood proactively notified Calypso about EdgePartners’ maintenance.

Proposed next steps:
1) Prepare an overlap timeline that shows (a) EdgePartners bulletin timestamps, (b) Calypso probe errors, (c) Redwood routing events, and (d) per-route latency/error buckets. I’ll export telemetry excerpt (redwood_telemetry_excerpt_20270610.csv).
2) Run the partial-degradation apportionment calc — we use a time-weighted availability model for blended events (we credit only for window where Redwood-originated faults are dominant). I’ll send the proposed credit calc for review.

I recommend we offer Calypso a good-faith partial credit while we finalize attribution; it’s better customer experience than a long dispute.

Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi Matthew — thanks for your patience. We completed an initial reconciliation and attached a short CSV with the proposed credit calculation (proposed_credit_calc_20270612.csv). Summary below: 

1) Timeline overlap: EdgePartners’ bulletin shows the control-plane activity beginning at 02:05:00Z. Calypso’s probes show elevated failures between 02:10:00Z and 02:43:00Z. Redwood telemetry confirms elevated errors and a routing fallback sequence between 02:09:40Z and 02:41:50Z localized to two POP groups that peer via EdgePartners.

2) Attribution: the window is blended. For ~55% of the impacted seconds, EdgePartners’ control-plane churn is the trigger; for ~45% of the impacted seconds, Redwood routing decisions and cache cold misses materially increased customer-experienced latency. Under our partial-degradation apportionment model we attribute 45% of the availability impact to Redwood.

3) Proposed credit: Calypso’s impacted window is 33 minutes. Our standard calculation pro-rates the monthly uptime credit for the impacted minutes and multiplies by the attribution share. Based on that approach, the preliminary credit amount is USD 1,850 (45% apportionment). We included the calculation sheet and the per-minute breakdown in the CSV.

4) Next steps: 
- Please confirm receipt of the proposed calc. If Calypso accepts, we’ll issue a formal credit memo against the June invoice and apply it within the next billing cycle.
- If you prefer further forensic evidence, we can schedule a joint session with EdgePartners and our network team to walk the routing traces and BGP timelines.

We want to be fair and transparent — if you’d like a temporary goodwill credit while the final forensic is performed, we can discuss that as well.

Apologies for the disruption and thanks for working through this with us.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
